_about: Day 14's tool-calling evaluation set. Two halves, because 'a tool call is correct'
means two different things at two different points in the pipeline:
routing     given a user's message, should an action be proposed AT ALL, and which?
validation  given a model's raw output, does a malformed proposal fail CLOSED?
WHO ROUTES, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE MODEL. Day 10 measured the generation model on the
routing decision and found constant functions: propose-v1 answered 'none' to all nine
cases including four explicit task requests, and a version with the none-anchoring
removed answered 'create-task' to all nine including 'what is the fleet size'. Neither
was deciding. Spring's keyword router with a question guard scored 8/9 with zero false
positives on the same set, so it owns the decision.
A FALSE POSITIVE IS THE EXPENSIVE ERROR. It puts a decision in front of a human that
should never have been raised, and a user cannot tell a guardrail from a broken
product. A miss merely does nothing. The set is weighted accordingly: more than a third
of the routing cases are traps built from the same vocabulary as real requests.
KNOWN GAP, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: summarize-document and lookup-knowledge are
published in GET /tools, validated by the contract, and executable since Day 11 — and
NOTHING EVER PROPOSES THEM. The keyword router only emits create-task. Cases for them
are marked unreachable_today so the set describes the goal while the numbers describe
